2023.DI3.2.t: Ensuring Safe and Accessible Pedestrian Routes in Construction Zones
2023.DI3.2.s: A presentation will be provided by Jennifer Niece, Acting Manager, Transportation Services Division on updating the city’s process to ensure safe and accessible routes in construction zones, including what recommendations were generated from stakeholder consultation and engagement.
2023.DI3.2.k: construction, pedestrians, safety; building, pedestrianization, public safety

m.x:
The Toronto Accessibility Advisory Committee recommends that the Infrastructure and Environment Committee recommend that:

1. City Council request the General Manager, Transportation Services to work with all constructors working in the transportation right-of-way, to ensure there is clear notification and signage, on which both 311 phone number and the construction zone number are listed, for all residents of Toronto regarding construction projects and the planned accommodations for safe, accessible, and clearly marked pedestrian routes through them.

2. City Council request the General Manager, Transportation Services to report back on related measures to the Toronto Accessibility Advisory Committee in the first quarter of 2024.

2023.DI4.3.t: Toronto Accessibility Advisory Committee 2024 Meeting Schedule
2023.DI4.3.s:
The Terms of Reference for the Toronto Accessibility Advisory Committee state that the Committee will hold up to six meetings per year at the call of the Chair or Vice-Chairs on delegation of the Chair.

The Chair has scheduled the following meetings for 2024:

Monday February 5, 2024, at 9:30 a.m.

Monday May 6, 2024, at 2:00 p.m.

Monday June 24, 2024, at 9:30 a.m.

Friday September 6, 2024, at 9:30 a.m.

Thursday October 17, 2024, at 9:30 a.m.

Wednesday December 11, 2024, at 9:30 a.m.

City Council on October 11 and 12, 2023, approved the 2024 schedule of meetings for City Council and its Committees. The schedule of meetings for Toronto Accessibility Advisory Committee has been developed to avoid dates, whenever possible, that conflict with the approved City Council schedule; and to avoid days of cultural or religious significance.
